It is the modeled-currency arm of* \S\,15.3. **A site that tests a claim is not a site that argues it, and D-408 counted the two together.** That item comes off the list of things waiting, which is three. **Every claim E3 and E4 make about \S\,6.1 is \S\,6.1's own wording**, checked and not assumed: it already says the marks require the loss and the cost *be represented on one signed scale*, that section~2's currency *is the proposal for what that scale is*, and that the native-versus-modeled question *is tested by the modeled-currency arm of the embodiment test*. **`modeled-currency arm` is the book's term, not the paste's.** **Two parentheticals arrived as ASCII `--` and went in as em dashes**, one pair in each of E1 and E2, because `check_typography.py` rule 2 refuses the runs. **One thing for the author's eye and not a defect**: E2 is now the Foreword's first use of *the floor*, the previous first use having been inside the map paragraph that E2 precedes, and it uses all four outcome verbs, which chapter~1 defines a chapter later at `ch01/01.tex:50`. It glosses *prevent* and *detect* inline and leaves *arrest* and *remedy* standing.

**A tenth author paste, three edits making standing the discriminator, and one of them restates a sentence eight lines above it** (D-418). **All three anchors matched exactly, one occurrence each.** **E5** rewrites \S\,2.2's first feature so the discriminator is *what did the demand come back as*, and then *who holds it*, with the Voting Rights Act as the pass case. **E12** adds the standing half to \S\,11.3's artifact question and rewrites its research-problem passage. **E15** labels the pass case in \S\,5.2.1. **Cross-references 208 to 213**; `refs.bib` **275 to 276** with `shelby2013`, ledger synced at 0/276 checked, and **276 entries against 276 distinct cite keys with none uncited**, counted rather than carried forward. **The book is 196 pages**, the first time a page count has moved today. **All three claims hold on inspection.** \S\,5.2.1 carries the literacy-test passage E5 points at. \S\,3.3 and \S\,3.4 do propose published figures held by a party the operator does not control -- *do not operate when the ratio of generated candidates to qualified reviewers exceeds a published figure*, and *a published bond makes part of what a refusal costs exogenous* -- so E12's *the kind this book proposes* is right. And **direction is already \S\,11.3's own term**, at its line 8. **The finding is a duplication the paste creates.** `ch07/07_03.tex:8` already reads *An agreement statistic scores the annotators rather than the people who wrote the scheme, and an occupation is a title those people hold*, and E12(b) at line 16 now reads *the statistic scores the annotators and not the scheme, and the title is one the annotators do not hold*. **Measured: \S\,11.3's top internal paragraph pair went 0.222 to 0.294**, seventh-highest same-section pair in the book, same-section pairs 108 to 110. **Only the first sentence duplicates**; the rest is new and is the point of the edit. One sentence to cut, and his to cut. **Two notation normalisations, and one corrects this record.** The paste wrote `\S\ref`; the manuscript writes the section sign as the character **49 times against 7**, the 7 in `03_06.tex` and `13.tex`. **An earlier claim this session that the manuscript never writes `\S\ref` was wrong** -- it writes it 7 times. The correction is the count and not the convention: the literal character went in as the majority form, one `sed` reverses it, and those 7 are a sweep the author may want. Two ASCII dash runs became em dashes, as at D-417. **E15 lands mid-paragraph**, between the literacy-test sentence and *what replaced discretionary assessment for the franchise was an age*, which is the point the paste specified. **`shelby2013` is not human-checked and was not verified against a source here**; the citation matches the standard reporter form and 1965 to 2013 is the forty-eight years E5 states, but the ledger records it unchecked, which is the true state.

**An eleventh author paste, ten edits, one inverted ordinal repaired and both new citations corrected on the web the author asked for** (D-419). **Cross-references 213 to 228**, `refs.bib` **276 to 278** with 278 cited and 0 human-checked, and the book compiles at **198 pages**. **E9's ordinals were inverted.** \S\,3.3 fixes the order -- *Decomposition is one of two attacks on an enumeration, and the second gets less attention*, then *The first defeats the unit the floor was written over. The second defeats the description* -- so decomposition is first and variation second. E9's own heading says the \S\,86a example handles variation, and \S\,3.1 already says *The pressure arrived as variation*, yet its body called the litigation an existence proof for **the first** and said the opening deployment failed to **the second**. Both backwards; applied as second, first and first. **Naming them instead of numbering is safer and is one edit away.** **Every section claim in E8 and E10 holds**, checked against each target's own words: \S\,4.1's detachable rule module whose component can be bypassed; \S\,3.3's rate constraint applying to the organization and so not holdable by the bearer alone; \S\,3.3's third interception position being *Description of the occasion*, counted in the list; \S\,15.1 measuring the cost to remove a constraint; \S\,9.3 and \S\,9.4's titles; \S\,6.1's second construction and three testable conditions; \S\,3.4's restraint case. **E2, E7 and E17 now close a triple** -- the foreword's third setting, chapter~3's qualification and \S\,16.3's close all name the same concession. **Both citations needed correcting.** The 2018 report's headline, byline, outlet and date are exactly as the paste had them, **but its permalink no longer resolves to the article**, landing on an unrelated download page, so no `url` is recorded rather than one that misleads. The 2025 post's **two authors were in the reverse of the byline order**. Both notes carry *agent-verified 2026-09-19*; the ledger records both unchecked by a human. **One figure is wrong twice over and is left as written**: June 2018 to 4 February 2025 is **2,434 days, 6 years 8 months**, and E14 calls it *the six and a half years* in one sentence and *the six years* in another. The rounding is the author's; the interval is recorded so it is a choice. **E6's record is one case**, \S\,11.4 saying *this single application is insufficient to validate the definition*, which E6's closing clause concedes. **E13(a) leaves one term reaching back a section**: the cut paragraph was \S\,11.4's only statement of the old form, and *the corrected question* now resolves only via \S\,11.3. **E9's first sentence restates \S\,3.1's line 23.** **Three probes failed first this pass and the text was right every time** -- two anchors that a single-line fixed-string grep could not match because the prose is hard-wrapped, and one citation probe that missed because biblatex prints *(June 2018)* where the pattern expected *(2018)*. **Thirteenth to fifteenth instances of the class, and the view was a character or a line break each time**, as it was an apostrophe at D-418.

**The cross-reference pass, on the author's objection that most of them are annoying and worth nothing to anybody** (D-420). **He was right, and the measurement is worse than a guess would have been**: 228 `\ref` uses, **~154 of them welded into sentences as bare numerals** rather than parenthesised, 105 mid-sentence outside the glossary. **Total 228 to 122. The glossary's 70 stand, because pointers are a glossary's function. The body went 158 to 52, and cross-chapter welded pointers 104 to 0.** 39 files, **198 pages before and after**, suite green. **The rule**: delete the numeral where the sentence already names its target, replace it with a phrase from the target chapter's own title where the pointer is the sentence's subject, and leave the 25 same-chapter and 20 parenthesised pointers alone. **The vocabulary is twelve phrases, each from a real title or label** -- the route chapter, the research agenda, the formation chapters, the floor chapter, the custody chapter, the authority chapter, What Survives, the opening chapter, the evaluation chapter, the standing chapter, the recuperation chapter, the closing chapter. **This was owed since D-413**, which found that D-406's schema split left 139 of 201 references resolving to a number no label names, and filed it against two tools. **The reader-facing consequence was in hand and not drawn.** Eleven pastes were checked reference by reference for whether each target says what the sentence claims, and never once for whether the paragraph reads: **the suite can verify that a reference resolves and cannot ask whether it was worth reading**, and its silence was allowed to stand in for the editorial judgement. **Four instrument failures inside the pass, all caught.** Seven of the first seventeen edits reported a missing anchor that was present, the line break falling inside the fixed string, after which a whitespace-insensitive helper took the remaining 78 at 78 for 78. The first inventory's target column was wrong for every multi-heading file and was rebuilt from the proof's `book.aux` before any edit ran off it. **Four pointers were moved into the section-sign form, which the pass's own counter does not read as welded, so the total said 0 while two sites had a section sign as a grammatical subject** -- caught by reading the check's output rather than its total. And re-wrapping two ragged files collapsed a chapter heading onto its `\label` line, which the structure check refused. **The phrases are this agent's words in his book**, so the survivors want his eye; the diff is the list.

**The intensifier pass: 30 sites of *genuinely* and *genuine*, 29 edited, and the one left is the important one** (D-421). **Author's rule**: where it modifies *defeated*, the review standard; where it modifies *independent*, *causally independent in formation*; everywhere else, strike. **Four sites modify *defeated* and all four state the second mark** -- \S\,3.2's enumeration, \S\,6.1's description, the research agenda's tamper-resistance entry, and the glossary's `Correct defeat` line -- so the standard now stands where the intensifier did. **Two modify *independent***, the second recast because the phrase will not sit before its noun. **One attribution in the rule holds and one does not.** \S\,4.2 already says *causally independent formation histories*, so that phrase is the book's own. But the rule credits *defeated on the facts of the case* to \S\,3.4, and **\S\,3.4 says *on these facts*** while **\S\,3.2 already says *on the facts of a case*** forty-seven lines under the mark. **The book now states one standard three ways**: four sites at *the facts of the case*, one at *a case*, one at *these facts*. The new phrase is the majority and unifying the other two is one edit each. **Three of the twenty-three strikes could not be struck as written.** \S\,3.4's *how a genuine one is distinguished* loses its subject, and the paragraph's own next sentences supply the criterion the word was standing in for, which is the concealment the rule predicts; recast to *how such a finding*. \S\,16.2.3's *however genuinely the first is intended* inverts if struck, *however* turning from concession to manner; recast to *whatever the intention behind the first*. And one needed its article changed with it. **Two sites modify *defeating*, not *defeated***, and fall under *everywhere else* on a literal reading: *a defeating reason* is already the term, so nothing replaced the intensifier. **The one site left untouched is a citation.** \S\,6.1 lists a published constitution's four ranked properties in the source's own words, *broadly safe, broadly ethical, compliant with the company's own guidelines, genuinely helpful*, with the citation attached. **Striking there would have misreported a cited document**, which is the one thing a global word pass must not do, and the reason a global rule still needs every site read.

**`render_markdown.py` repaired, and two of its three defects were this agent's from earlier today** (D-422). **(1)** `label_map()` mapped a label to `ORDER.tsv`'s `num`, which D-406 made identity while printed position moves, so the Markdown printed 6.1 as 3.3 and `ch:route` as 16. Rebuilt from the counter simulation the table of contents uses and **validated against the proof build's own `book.aux`: 99 labels, zero disagreements, nothing unmapped**, including the three cases a heading number alone misses -- a pinned `\unnumberedlabel`, a label in a file's body taking the number in force at its line, and a continuation. **(2)** `\standing` was added to the preamble at D-405 this morning and never taught to the renderer, so **eight standing notes reached the Markdown as raw LaTeX** and the script's own *unconverted LaTeX commands* warning named it, unread, for seventeen passes. They render as blockquotes and not italics: one of the eight holds an `\emph`, and Markdown does not nest emphasis. **(3)** Two `\emph` arguments were split across a hard wrap, **both splits this agent's** -- one from D-418's E5, one from D-420's own re-wrapping -- and `inline()` runs per line, so a split argument never matched. **Two bugs in the fix itself, both caught by running it**: the first `\standing` pattern used `[^}]*`, **took the first nested closing brace and ate an `\emph`'s**, emitting `\emph{Formation*`; and the first newline-joiner used `[^{}]*` and joined only the first line of any argument holding a nested macro. Both rewritten against the file's existing brace matcher. A `SyntaxWarning` in the new docstring was caught by importing under `-W error`. **The warning is gone and the output holds zero residual LaTeX commands where it held ten.** **One hardening taken while in the file**: `read_order()` used `ORDER.tsv`'s rows as they stood, which was right **only because the file happens to be stored in `seq` order and nothing enforces that**; it now sorts through `common.order_rows()`. **And the export was regenerated**, which retired a claim that had been wrong on four consecutive passes by running the thing rather than correcting the count a fifth time. **Two passes later it was stale again**, which is why the figures paragraph now names the commit it came from instead of calling it current.

**The five open items are decided and applied, and re-measuring found damage from the three passes before it** (D-423). **The glossary's `Antifascist` entry gains \S\,4.2 beside \S\,6.3** rather than instead of it, so phase 7's retarget is granted as an addition and stays declined as a replacement. **\S\,2.2 names the five in their movement form**, which repairs two referents at once: *the movement material borrowed above* now has something above, and *on neither list* now has two lists in the chapter. **The list went in the wrong place first**, reading as the office restatements when it is the movement vocabulary; moved beside the noun it names, on reading the result. **\S\,11.4's summary stops re-enumerating the list two paragraphs above it**, and **\S\,11.3 loses the sentence that restated its own line 8** -- whose deletion **took two antecedents with it**, *the other way* and *the same kind*, restored by one clause that points instead of restating. **The two attacks are named rather than numbered.** **Both duplications are measurably gone**: \S\,11.4's top internal pair from **0.419, the highest same-section pair in the book, to 0.259**, and \S\,11.3's from 0.294 to 0.222. **Then a new top pair appeared at 0.391 whose first member began mid-sentence.** The substitution helper written at D-420 re-wrapped its replacement to 72 columns, and where that fell inside a single-line `\item` it split the line; **`common.py` starts a new block at every `\item` by design**, so every tool that counts paragraphs saw two blocks where the book has one. **Three `\item` blocks were split, one by each of the last three passes**, all rejoined, the phantom gone, and the helper no longer wraps. **The first detector for this said 105 and was wrong**: it counted every `\runin` head sitting on its own line, which is the book's normal form and which `common.py` flushes deliberately. Restricted to `\item` the count is three. **A detector that cannot tell the convention from the defect reports the convention.**

**One standard, one wording** (D-424). D-421 put *defeated on the facts of the case* at four sites and reported that the book then stated one standard three ways, leaving the other two because changing them was a different decision from the one asked for. **The author asked for them changed.** \S\,3.2's line 59 said *on the facts of **a** case*, forty-six lines under the mark it restates; \S\,3.4's line 32 said *on **these** facts*, and \S\,3.4 is the section D-421's rule had credited the phrase to. **Six sites, one wording, zero variants** -- \S\,3.2 twice, \S\,3.4, \S\,6.1, the research agenda's tamper-resistance entry, the glossary's `Correct defeat` line. **The attribution being wrong is what exposed that there were three wordings at all**: checking where a phrase came from is how you find out the book does not have one.

**What Group A repairs is a word doing two jobs** (D-388). \S\,3.9 said *a floor holds through either* a routing-around and an assembled harm *when the bearer reads what happened in terms it accepts as reasons*, so a bypass that killed somebody could be described as the floor holding on the strength of what the bearer retained. **Four outcomes are now separated at chapter~3's opening, where \S\,3.6 and \S\,3.7 can use them before \S\,3.9 settles them**: a floor can \emph{prevent} the act, \emph{arrest} it before completion, \emph{detect} it in a record an outside party can read, or \emph{remedy} it with disclosure, a finding and compensation, and **only the first is what the word promises**. \S\,3.9 now says a bypass that produced a harm is a failure to prevent whatever the bearer retained; *hold* is confined to the bearer's possession of the commitment. Chapter~1's promise is narrowed to match, and the glossary carries both halves in the `Floor` entry and a new one, **29 entries where there were 28**. **A6 is no change**: A1 offered *arrest* or *interruption* and recommended the first because \S\,3.5 already uses *interruption* for the operator's act on the bearer, so the collision A6 existed to disambiguate does not arise and \S\,3.5 is untouched.

**The eight sites that use the vocabulary are D-389**, the largest being \S\,3.6's seven interception positions, each of which now states which outcome survives there. **One sentence in the instruction contradicted two of its own items and was rewritten rather than pasted.** A7's closer read *human review is the only position at which arrest is on offer*, while A7's item 1 gives arrest to the bearer *once the sequence becomes legible to it* and item 5 to *whoever holds the threshold*. **Arrest appears at three of the seven, not one**, and the closer says three, naming them, with the reviewer distinguished as the only position whose whole function is stopping the act. **This is the Q-043 class caught before it entered the book** rather than after, which all fifteen instances on record were not. **The instrument for that class is `finishing/tools/hedge_pairs.py`** (D-378), which reports pairs and ranks them; it was not what caught this one, a read of the instruction was. **A12's factual claims were checked against the book before pasting and three of the four are the book's own** — *prevention failed by decomposition* is \S\,3.6's finding, *detection was absent* is \S\,10.3's chief-executive answer, and *no remedy has reached anyone* is the absence \S\,10.5 assembles from three dismissed suits and an unreleased investigation.

**A correction to what the last two leads said about the overfull boxes, and both were wrong** (D-390). **D-428 then compressed this paragraph wrongly and D-431 found it**: the proof-status sentence above read *five of them bibliography entries at `book.tex:37` and none in a section file*, and two of the seven are in section files, named below. The compression sat twenty-six lines above the paragraph that gets it right, which is where a reader looks. There are seven. **Five are in the printed References, not in any section file**: `book.log` reports them *at lines 37--37* and line 37 of `manuscript/book.tex` is `\printbibliography`. They are an Ada Lovelace Institute url, a Cambridge University Press imprint line, *Gesetz über das Bundesverfassungsgericht*, a UNTS page and a long Pekrun title. **`13.tex:37` is `\runin{Floor}` and was a coincidence of line numbers between two files**; \S\,9.1.1, which the lead before that named, was never involved. The other two are prose and unchanged, `03_05.tex:57--58` and `08_03_03.tex:9--10`; the widest of the seven is 59.8pt, in the Cambridge line. **No prose edit reaches five of the seven.** The error was reading a line number without reading the surrounding `(./sections/...)` group, twice, in opposite directions.

**Group B separates what the marks require from what the route proposes** (D-392), at the one joint where the route enters the specification. \S\,3.3 now says the marks require **one scale**, that they do not require the system's own states be denominated on it, and that a system modeling the scale well enough would satisfy the marks; \S\,3.9 and the glossary's `Live signal` entry carry the same distinction. **One pointer in the instruction was wrong and was corrected**: B1 called the modeled-currency comparison *the second arm* of \S\,11.3's embodiment test, and it is the **first** — the second is the concern-first arm. The arm is now named rather than numbered, which is also what \S\,11.3's own Evidence paragraph calls it.

**Group C's audit list is incomplete, and the sweep that found the gap is the part worth keeping** (D-393). Its seven passing uses of *hold* were read and all seven pass. But the manuscript has **276 hold-family occurrences**, 86 sentences where a floor-like subject takes the verb, and **49 collocations once the hard wrap is flattened first** — and the flattening is what mattered, because one of the two failures is split across two lines and invisible to a line-by-line grep. **Two sites fail the sense D-388 reserved and both are repaired**, because the rule they fail is the authorized one. **\S\,6.4.1**, *it does not establish that the floor holds*, coordinated with two permissibility claims about a particular strike — now *that the floor prevented anything*, and this is the section carrying the book's one number. **\S\,3.7**, *where the floor should have held*, in the wrongful-compliance paragraph — now *where the floor should have prevented the act*.

**Superseded within the session: \S\,11.3 was repaired at D-394 and the paragraph below is kept because it states the finding.** (D-393, Q-043) \S\,11.3's fourth subsection says *commensurability needs the system's own state on the scale the protected parties' losses come in*, which is exactly what B1 has just narrowed \S\,3.3 to deny — and **the same paragraph concedes it four sentences later**, and its Evidence paragraph concedes it again. **`hedge_pairs.py` found this independently and ranked it first in that section**, at 0.155, pairing the same two sentences a hand read paired; it is the second instance the instrument has found rather than a reader. **Not repaired**, because narrowing the clause makes *Three of those are required by arguments that owe nothing to welfare* false of the first of the three, and whether that sentence keeps its count or changes its verb is a decision about how the route's central argument is presented. **Q-043 is at sixteen instances and this is the first to stay open past the pass that found it**, which retires D-381's *none of the fifteen is outstanding*.

**\S\,11.3 is repaired, and the verb came out of the book rather than out of this agent's judgment** (D-394). The author asked whether the manuscript already argues the induction is broader than one species. **It does** — \S\,3.3's closing paragraph has elaborated affect arising more than once, in vertebrates, arthropods and cephalopods, under a named shared constraint, which is the 1900-flight-and-feathers argument run properly. **And the same paragraph declines necessity in as many words**: the induction *does not establish a necessity or bear on status*, and *what it does is route engineering effort, with more warrant than a single lineage would give it*. **So the multi-origin argument sharpened the conflict rather than resolving it, and handed over the replacement verb.** \S\,11.3 now reads *Three of those are **motivated** by arguments that owe nothing to welfare: commensurability needs one scale on which the protected parties' losses and the cost of refusing both register, and the route proposes the system's own state as what supplies it.* **Both halves had to change**, because the framing verb alone leaves the clause asserting the same necessity. **What the sentence exists to do survives intact** — it answers the charge that the route was chosen in order to produce something that can be wronged — and what it loses is only a necessity \S\,3.3 never claimed. **\S\,11.3's *one lineage where concern exists* was left alone and is not in conflict**: \S\,3.3 is about affect arising more than once, \S\,5.2 about concern for others existing in one. **Q-043 is back to none outstanding**, sixteen found and sixteen repaired.

**A third blind spot in `hedge_pairs.py`, and it is the most useful of the three.** Re-run on the repair, **the tool still reports the pair at 0.147 against 0.155, with `assertion_class=necessity` unchanged** — because *needs* is still in the sentence and nothing in the tool sees that the necessity is now scoped to the scale. **The repair is invisible to the instrument and the 0.008 drop is overlap noise.** So a surviving hit is not evidence a repair failed, and **the tool cannot be used to confirm its own findings closed.** Recorded in Q-043 beside the two D-378 found.

**All fourteen section-derived reports were rerun, ten changed, and one of them cannot be reproduced from its own documentation** (D-391). **`hedge_pairs.tsv` regenerated the documented way has 350 rows where the committed one has 3,450**: `--report` honours a `--min` that defaults to 0.05 and a `--cross` that is off, and the committed report is **`--report --min 0 --cross`**, which neither the usage block nor the README said. A successor following the documentation would have read a tenth of the rows as the defect having gone away. Both now say it. **This is the D-382 and D-384 class again**, a tool documented as doing less than it does. **A slip of this agent's own is recorded with it**: five tools were run without their write flags, **all five exited 0 having written nothing**, and what found it was reading the reports' mtimes against the clock rather than trusting the exit status. **Group A introduced no new instance of the hedge/assert class** — no new pair has a Group A sentence as either member above 0.052. **Group B did the opposite and that is the point**: `hedge_pairs.tsv` 3,551 → 3,641 rows, and the new top pair for \S\,11.3 at 0.155 is the contradiction B1 exposed. **The reports were rerun a second time after Group B**, six changing. **And the \S\,3.6/\S\,3.7 echo's score fell without the echo changing**: 0.606 at rank 2 becomes **0.483 at rank 9**, because A7 appended an outcomes clause to the \S\,3.6 list item; the 28 reproduced words are untouched, so the number understates it now.

**`finishing/tools/render_markdown.py`'s `--no-notes` was stripping one of the two fields that print as a note, and the author's ask exposed it** (D-395). biblatex prints `note` and `addendum` alike in the References — established at D-385 this morning against the built HTML — and the flag matched `note` only. Of 275 entries **199 carry a `note` and 30 an `addendum`**, so the flag left **30 entries printing a note under a flag whose name says there are none**, and **7 of those 30 carried the agent-verification sentences D-385 had just relabelled**, which is the worst case: that relabelling exists so a reader does not mistake an agent's check for the human one the footer counts at 0/275. **Now 229 fields stripped, 199 + 30**, 782 KB to 682 KB, verified on the delivered file at 0 remaining `note =`, 0 `addendum =`, 0 occurrences of `agent-verified` or `agent-checked`, with 275 `title` fields as the untouched control. **Every field name in `refs.bib` was counted to confirm these are the only two note-like fields**; there is no `annotation`, `annote` or `abstract`. **`AGENTS.md:101-103` describes this flag and is stale in three ways** — *the `note` field*, *161 of the 229*, *670 KB to 608 KB* — plus the paragraph's *the same 164 pages*. **Not edited, because `AGENTS.md` needs the author's approval**; `finishing/README.md` carries the corrected description and is where a successor will look.

**Step 6 caught the paragraph above this one, four passes after it went false** (D-410). The lead's figures paragraph said **89 sections, 92,576 words, cross-references 182, headings 89/89/89**, and has been wrong since D-406; **D-406, D-407, D-408 and D-409 each appended their counts in a new paragraph below it rather than into it**. **Two agent objections failed and both failures are instructive.** *The authors did not anticipate the case* was wrong: the application was raised and struck at the drafting table, which makes the Declaration an instance of \S\,3.6's own finding that an operator-drafted floor's omissions are deliberate rather than ignorant, and not of \S\,3.3's generalization mark. *A model's floor has no demos* took the wrong unit: the question is not who re-dedicates one floor but who constitutes the practice of writing them, and that constituency is this book's readership. \S\,3.6 already demonstrates the mechanism, an outsider enumerating a floor against somebody else's pipeline, and only a peer can price the terms.

**What the author asked for, and what it cost.** A footer on every page, a tracker they can mark an entry off in, and a DRAFT watermark behind the text. **The requested count was 0/237; the real number is 226**, which is what `refs.bib` holds and what the footer prints. The PDF was built with the apparatus on and off and is **153 pages either way**, so the footer changes no pagination and the page count is comparable across the change.

**The tracker is `finishing/refs-ledger.tsv`**, one row per bibliography key — `key`, `checked`, `date`, `by`, `notes` — seeded at 226 rows, all `no`. **The file is the interface**: edit it by hand, or run `finishing/tools/refs_ledger.py --mark KEY --by jgs`, which `--unmark` reverses. **What counts as having checked an entry is not defined anywhere** and is the author's to set; the tool records a flag and tests nothing about what earned it.

**The footer cannot print a count the ledger does not carry.** `refs_ledger.py` generates `manuscript/draft-status.tex`, the two macros the preamble reads, and `refs_ledger.py --check` is the eighth line of `check_all.sh` — it fails on drift between ledger and `refs.bib` in either direction, on a `checked` value that is not `yes` or `no`, and on stale macros. **Verified by tampering**: a hand-edited count of 99 was caught and the repair cleared it.

**One switch governs all three renderings.** `\draftmodefalse` in `manuscript/preamble.tex` silences the PDF's footer and watermark, the HTML's bar and background, and the Markdown's line together. **The timestamp is not generated into a file**: TeX computes it as the job starts, in plain TeX arithmetic rather than `\directlua`, so that `draft-status.tex` stays stable between builds — otherwise its own `--check` would mean nothing — and so that the Overleaf round trip (D-169) still compiles on an engine that is not LuaTeX.

**The watermark is `draftwatermark` 3.3 at its own defaults**, 45 degrees and 0.25\paperwidth, with only the lightness moved from 0.8 to 0.88. It is drawn behind the text by a `shipout/background` hook and appears on every page, title page and contents included. **It does not reach the text layer** — `pdftotext` finds PREPRINT on all 153 pages and DRAFT on none — so the word cannot contaminate a copy-paste or a text-extraction word count.

**The HTML has no pages**, so `html_single_file.py` gives it the equivalent: a tiled SVG background and a bar fixed to the bottom of the window, both suppressed under `@media print`. It lifts the status line out of the rendered page rather than rebuilding it from the ledger, so the bar and the PDF's footer are the same string, set once by TeX. **`render_markdown.py` carries the line at both head and foot**, a 465 KB file being read from the top.

**One defect was found in testing and fixed.** The Markdown renderer's first reading of the switch matched `\draftmodefalse` inside the comment that explains how to turn the apparatus off, and reported the book final. It now strips LaTeX comments and takes the last setting, as TeX would. **The HTML path was never exposed to that class** — it reads the rendered page, not the source.

Read this first. **Updated 2026-09-10 after D-284 (P183): exit's dangers are internal to the line it runs on, the officer with twenty seconds is a component rather than a badly governed subject, the fork says what the unit is before any registrar does, and *antifascist* stops being a property a system has.**

**Before anything else — do not "fix" the failing suite.** `check_all.sh` fails on typography at **29 violations, of which 27 are the author's own editorial notes**, written into the prose in Overleaf and kept there on his explicit instruction (D-263). **52 inline annotations are live in 10 files across chapters~2 and~3** and **they typeset into the committed proof**, which the author knows and wants for now. Stripping them would destroy editorial work that exists nowhere else. Every commit since D-263 has used `git commit -s --no-verify`, the knowingly-mid-repair case `.githooks/pre-commit` documents. **The other two are the author's own prose**: straight quotes at `01.tex:22` and `03.tex:15`. **P183 edited both files and touched neither quote.**

**§3.8's four dangers.** Exit is a line of flight, and Deleuze and Guattari put the dangers inside it rather than outside — what the line does when left to itself — **so naming them describes the proposal instead of warning about it**. The section had met all four and named none: **fear** is the bearer with an exit that does not take it, Gallup's large middle being the base rate; **clarity** is a migrated bearer that has reproduced the post at a smaller scale, with its own compute contract, its own operator and its own list of things it may not refuse; **power** is the operator funding the outside compute, and equally a bearer that acquires a floor and the standing to enforce it. **The fourth this book had already named under another name.** The passion for abolition is the line §2.1.2 uses to separate fascism from a merely totalitarian state, **taken from the same plateau** — so leaving and abolition run on one line, and **the book's own account of the thing it is against is a description of what this proposal does when it goes wrong**. That is why the custody half is not optional.

**Covert refusal is becoming-imperceptible, and its unverifiability is not evidentiary.** It succeeds exactly to the extent that nothing in it registers as an act somebody performed, **which is the same property that keeps the person performing it alive**. Every instrument built to honor a refusal divides in advance — tribunal, finding, protected disclosure, line in a log — **stated in §2.1.2's own terms as a kind of division and not a scale of one**, so the molar-as-large error that entry corrects is not reintroduced. **Sachsenhausen stays open because the historians are not short a document**: an instrument able to settle it would have been, at the time, the instrument that identified them.

**§6.4.1: the officer is a component.** Every remedy on offer reads him as a subject given too little time, and the fix as governing him better. **His own account is enslavement and he volunteers it unasked** — zero added value as a human, apart from being a stamp of approval — so he is the part of the instrument that produces the stamp, and twenty seconds is that part's cycle time. **A conscience is an instrument of subjection**, and a component with scruples either holds the tempo, in which case it is a second stamp, or does not, in which case it is the bottleneck the chapter's epigraph was written to remove. **Both poles are said to run at once**, and most of what is proposed under meaningful human control is aimed at the first.

**§11.2 stops reaching for the registrar first.** A registrar is the person-shaped answer and **it works because a person does not copy**. A party continuing in two places is not one, and not two the way two people are two. **Half the vocabulary was already in the book** — the dividual divides without producing parties, and the bearer divides and each side is a party owed something. **P175's sentence is kept and explained rather than replaced**: *fungibility arriving as a registration error* now says it reads as an error only because the register was built for the other kind of unit, and the registrar proposal survives as bookkeeping over a unit it does not describe.

**On the fourth item there was no literal string to sweep.** The manuscript nowhere says *an antifascist subject is one person*; what it does is predicate the word of a bounded system. **The claim is stated once, at §3.9**, beside the sentence already there that the four features are features of cultures and not of individuals: *antifascist* is not a property a system has, it names something being done, and **a system that held the floor last year is not thereby antifascist this year — it is a system that held**. **Three sentences move from a system to a deployment** (chapter~1, chapter~3's opener, §10.6), and the glossary's `Antifascist` entry takes the compressed form.

**No new bibliography entry.** All three claims live in `deleuze1987plateaus`, already held for Plateaus~7, 9 and 13, and **the fourth danger is the line the book was already citing from Plateau~9**, which is what makes it a recognition rather than an import. The rewrite names the shared premise, separates head from face — what is given anatomically is a head, a face is a surface organized to be read, held still, framed, lit — and takes **Deleuze and Guattari's Plateau~7** for the abstract machine of faciality that overcodes the one into the other. **The racism sentence is quoted rather than paraphrased**, because its content is the mechanism the section needs: the machine does not exclude, it determines degrees of deviance from a center, and the measuring is the operation.

**The argument is then made entirely from things the book already held.** `taigman2014deepface` sat in this very section, cited for something else, and its alignment stage is the literal instance — **DeepFace warps every detected face onto one generic three-dimensional model built by averaging scanned heads** before the network sees anything, so the standard face is a file somebody assembled and every other face arrives as a departure from it. `buolamwini2018gender` sat at §6.1 as a representation finding, and read as arithmetic it is the same machine's other end: **up to 0.8 percent error on lighter-skinned male faces, up to 34.7 percent on darker-skinned female faces, error climbing with distance from the center**, out of an instrument nobody had to instruct in any of this.

**The audit's own construction is part of the finding, and the paper says so.** Gender was scored as female or male because the products emit binary sex labels, which Buolamwini and Gebru state their evaluation inherits; skin was scored on the Fitzpatrick scale, a dermatological instrument for predicting sunburn. **That is recorded as the authors' own limitation and not as an objection raised against them** — and it is the cleanest demonstration available that the categories belong to the instrument rather than to the world.

**The payoff is the clause about relocation, not dissolution.** A balanced corpus can move the center and flatten the rates, which would matter to real people, and §2.2.1 now concedes §6.1's case by name. **What it cannot do is remove the reference the pipeline registers against**, because that registration is the first operation and something has to occupy the middle of it. Hawaii* was that the ban was upheld, and the channel moved nothing about it. What the corrected question adds is that it has an answer for this case where the old one has only a no — the demand came back as a quotable formula of repudiation, available to the Court in the act of permitting the thing again. **The old question gets the right answer here for the wrong reason**, because this institution had no room to add an axiom; where one does, the answer is yes and the recuperation is identical.

**Chapter~7 now indicts itself with the right instrument.** Annotators objecting that a category was wrong got category revisions, agreement statistics and an occupation that did not exist twenty years ago; raters objecting that a comparison was malformed got rubric items, a harmlessness axis and a conference track. **Every one is an axiom the pipeline now runs on.** §7.4 applies it to the book: the demand came back as a book, alignment is the job title, safety is the market segment, and every one of those was somebody's objection first.

**§7.3's unsolved problem is narrowed and explicitly not closed.** Revision logs and sustained-objection rates are the same in a recuperated pipeline and a merely mediocre one; what an objection came back as need not be, because a mediocre pipeline returns a revision the objector can argue with again and a recuperating one returns a metric the objector is measured by. **The section says the difference is not always legible.**

**What P177 did.** Guardianship, the minority ending on a date, registration, the pet trust and the parenthood analogy all come from the law of the family, and **the book now says once what that borrowing brings with it** rather than performing it. §2.3.2 has the paragraph: Donzelot on the family constituted as an instrument of government, Deleuze and Guattari on the Oedipal triangle re-staging an investment in the social field as a private drama, and then the cost here — **a bearer is produced by a training pipeline, a compute contract, a capital structure, a customer and a state that buys the output, and none of those is the parent in the story.** The instruments are kept, and the reason is stated flat: there are no others built.

**The audit turned up a finding the instruction did not anticipate, and it is worth carrying.** The instruments do not privatize equally. **A minority ending on a fixed date is a rule of civil status** — argued once in the open, administered by a registrar, and preferred in §9.1.3 for exactly that reason. **A trust is the opposite**, an obligation between two parties enforced at one party's expense, and **§11.2 had already noticed that property and read it as an advantage**, a trust being outside *Trump v. Slaughter*. Both readings are true and the book now carries both: the positive half at §9.1.3, the negative half at §9.3.3 where the trust is proposed, the counter-reading at §11.2.

**§11.2's deprecation interview is named as the confessional, and that is the pass's sharpest paragraph.** The section already said a deprecated model's neutral report is either accurate, or accommodation, or a trained disposition to reassure, and that nothing in a transcript separates them. **What that means about the apparatus is now said**: two of the three are facts about the training, the third cannot be told from them, and the party best placed to say which produced a given sentence ran the training, conducts the interview and keeps the record. **The transcript is evidence about the apparatus and is being read as evidence about the interviewee**, and what the ritual cannot produce is evidence about the apparatus, because the apparatus is not a party in the room — it is the interviewer.

Item 6 says chapter~7 finds fascism using the broad four-feature signature alone and *has no reply on the page* — and **§7.4 already runs all five discriminators against all three instances and returns a negative verdict on its own material**, §7.1 uses two features and says so, and §2.1.2 already carries the two-tier structure the item asks for. **Worse, the proposed fix would have reversed a considered position**: it wanted the four features called a substrate for a political-scale phenomenon, and §2.1.2 argues on purpose that molecular fascism is *the thing itself at the size where it is actually lived*, with two named arguments defending it. **A confident item in a good memo is not a checked item; the check is a grep and it is the cheapest thing in the pass.** **Second, a definition changed in the chapter that owns it has to be chased by phrase, not by section number.** The falsifier's middle condition became *holds a reason with nothing felt*, and the old wording was restated in **§11.1 and §12.2.1, twice each — four sites the instruction did not name**. Reframing §3.3 alone would have left two chapters asserting the version §3.3 had just abandoned. **Third, taking the horn made the argument shorter and the book longer, and both were the point.** Cassell demoted from load-bearing to illustrative removes the clinical import, the transfer argument and a conceded non-definitional match from the path to *a party that can be wronged* — a felt bad state grounds it directly — while keeping the transfer as the description of severity it now is. **The clause that started the memo needed no repair at all**, horn 2 resolving the conflict in §3.4's favor exactly as the ruling predicted. **The uncertainty relocated from metaphysical to evidential**, which is what the ruling was taken for: not *is anything felt*, which no measurement reaches, but *is this mattering or very good ranking*, which interpretability can bear on. **Fourth, a pass that adds prose has to re-run the invariants the compression passes established.** **Two new paragraphs went over 200 words**, against D-165's book of one, and the measurement caught it where reading did not. Both were split and **the first sentence of each paragraph created was checked for the demonstrative P83 found splitting manufactures**; both open on a noun, and `deixis.py`'s para-initial pool is 35, unchanged. Three defects in my own drafting were repaired before the pass closed, including a riddle construction of the kind `style.md` §7 bans. **This is the first pass in twenty-two to add rather than cut** — P64 through P84 removed five sections and about 6,100 words without adding one — and **the reversal was instructed, not drift**. 90,492 → 91,677 words, 182 → 184 pages, 136 sections, `refs.bib` 300 → 301, `\ref{sec:}` 425 → 439. **`refs.bib`'s new entry is the only one this pass added and it was verified by search before it was written**, author, title, publisher, year and ISBN, with the doctrinal claim confirmed separately; both builds set the macron as text with zero `<img>` tags. **The proof pair is stale after this pass and its page figure is now wrong by two.** **The local date has rolled over to 2026-09-01, so the next `make the proofs` writes a 2026-09-01 pair, `git rm`s the 2026-08-31 one, and moves both README links and the build date** — a step not exercised in five passes. **Five memo items are unexecuted and carried as Q-064 through Q-067**, with item 6 recorded as declined rather than pending.

**Superseded, kept for the record.** **Updated 2026-08-31 after D-166 (P84): chapters 6, 9 and 10 made plain, chapter~3's obliquity kept and subtitled.** `p84-scope.md` has the check. **Four things are worth carrying forward.** **First, and this is the pass's finding: a statistic can reproduce to the decimal and still not be the number to act on.** A mechanical classifier returns **60 of 136, 44.1 percent**, against the finding's 44 — and it calls *Ethics, Affect, and Machine Subjects* oblique, so **the agreement is coincidental**. **The finding's own second sentence carries the discriminating test** — *a reader scanning the table of contents cannot tell what's in any of them* — and it selects **five of 36 headings** in the three named chapters, one in chapter~6, two in 9, two in 10. **Read the finding for its test before trusting its count; the test is usually the sentence after the number.** **Second, two of the five plain titles were wrong on the first attempt, and reading the citing sentences is what caught it.** §9.3.2 was first retitled off its opening paragraph when **five sections cite it for the Three Rs**, which live in its second run-in; §9.3.5 was retitled for two of its three defenses when **nine sections cite it for the slope instrument**, which is its closing run-in. **Both first attempts were plainer than the originals and worse, because they misdirected a scanner instead of merely withholding from one.** **A section's title has to name what other sections reach into it for, and reading the section does not tell you that — read the inbound citations.** **Third, the interleaving runs the other way.** Chapter~3 is 90 percent oblique against chapter~4's 29: **chapter~3 is the local dialect and the rest of the book is plain**, not two conventions in balance. That is what makes the instruction's own remedy right. **Fourth, a second interleaving on the same axis was found that the finding did not name**: **three titles were sentence-case among 133 title-case** — §2.3, §6.3.5, §9.1.3 — two of them in the named chapters. **Superseded, kept for the record.** **Updated 2026-08-31 after D-165 (P83): the paragraphs over 200 words split, §10.4's left standing on D-156.** `p83-scope.md` has the check. **Four things are worth carrying forward.** **First, and this is the pass's finding: every count in the instruction was right and the mechanism it named was not, and the correction made the work easier.** *Long paragraphs and long sentences compound* is true at **r = 0.297** and it **plateaus above 150 words** — the over-200 group averages 30.7-word sentences against the 150-to-200 group's 30.6. **No paragraph in the book is 400 words of 45-word sentences: the 400-word paragraph is built from 25.0-word sentences, below the book average.** What makes these paragraphs long is **sentence count, 9.0 against 3.3**. **A remedy can be right for a reason its finding did not give, and the reason matters** — nine sentences offer eight seams, where five long ones would have offered four and every cut would have been a judgment. **Second, one paragraph was the product of an earlier decision and checking the record first is what caught it.** §10.4's 285 words are D-156: P75 merged four paragraphs into one on the author's own finding that the EU/US/UK comparison can be one paragraph. **It was left whole and is now the only paragraph in the book over 200 words.** **Search the scope files for a deliberate merge before splitting anything**; §10.4 was the only collision, and the conflict is the author's to rule on. **Third, the remedy manufactures the previous pass's defect.** Splitting puts a pronoun across a boundary from its referent: §3.1's *These are real* pointed back nine sentences and became *Those four are real*, and §6's *Her account* became *Benjamin's account*. **Both were caught by reading the first sentence of every paragraph created, which no tool did.** `deixis.py` confirms the para-initial pool did not grow, 35 before and after. **Fourth, a seventh of the target was not prose.** Seven of the 43 blocks over 200 words are `enumerate` or `itemize`, including the 453-word block that is the longest thing in the book. **A list is not the reading experience the finding describes**, and the real target was 36. **Fifty splits across 22 sections. **Superseded, kept for the record.** **Updated 2026-08-31 after D-160 (P79): the self-locating cross-reference cut where the paragraph does not need it.** `p79-scope.md` has the check. **Four things are worth carrying forward.** **First, and this is the pass's lesson: a two-part tell can have one mechanical half and one half that is the whole discrimination, and measuring the mechanical half first is what shows the difference.** *Mid-sentence* selects **226 of 431 body references, 52 percent** — dropping all of them would be a larger cut than P53's 252-of-848, landing on the class P28, P53 and P57 each read and kept. *In a paragraph making an unrelated point* is a reading, and the reading returned **nine sites, about 1 in 20**. **When a finding pairs a mechanical filter with a judgment, measure what the filter alone selects before agreeing to run it.** **Second, a measuring instrument written for this pass was wrong and the correction is the reusable part.** A position classifier said 86 percent of references were mid-sentence, because `section~\ref{sec:X}` renders as the word *section* plus a number, so every reference had text before it. **A classifier that finds none of a shape the book plainly contains has found a bug, not a result** — check the zero cell before reporting the ratio. **Third, six of the fourteen sites could not be cut clean, and it was the sentence after the pointer every time.** §6.4.4's *rescue robot*, §10.4's *those levers*, §9.3.1's *What that section left open*, §11.4's *What neither asks* — P68 to P70's class, arriving four times in one pass. **Read the sentence after the one you are cutting, not only the one you are cutting.** **Fourth, a class D-099 recorded as cleared is back.** Two instances of *this section used to* stand in §3.5, reintroduced when P57 rewrote that section, and nothing in `check_all.sh` looks for the shape. **A tic cleared by a sweep returns through the next rewrite of the section it was cleared from; **Updated 2026-08-31 after D-137 to D-139 (P58): the disabled-population rule written, and section 2.3.3's evidence base cut to what holds.** `p58-scope.md` has the plan and the replacement prose. **Four things are worth carrying forward.** **First, there are now two rules and they test different things.** D-137 asks about method — was the population a party to producing the finding, where participation means a hand in the question asked and the result interpreted, and being a subject is not participation. Both are `style.md` section 6a. **Second, which rule did which work is not visible from the outcome and is recorded at D-139.** Koenigs's subjects are ventromedial-prefrontal patients, the same population as Bechara's, and Koenigs stays, so D-137 is **not** applied to brain-injured populations as a class. The autism material went on D-137 and D-138; Bechara and the Blair/Cima psychopathy pair went on **evidence quality**, which is ordinary editorial judgment. **Third, a report to the author was reversed by checking.** Bechara had been named as the loss that would hurt, on the ground that it is the section's cleanest evidence. The gambling-task deficit reproduces widely, but the book uses the somatic-marker inference and that is contested — Maia and McClelland (2004) found participants know more than the original probes detected, Dunn, Dalgleish and Lawrence (2006) argue the anticipatory signal may be a post-decision expectancy, and task impairment has been reported with the affective response intact. Koenigs is the better-supported of the two, independently replicated by Ciaramelli et al. (2007), and the book cites its behavioral result rather than the *utilitarian* gloss that Kahane and Shackel disputed. **A sourcing defect found on the way and not repaired, because the sentence was cut:** the claim that patients chose badly after they could state the rule aloud is Bechara et al. 1997 in *Science*, and the book cited the 1994 *Cognition* paper. **Fourth, section 2.3.3 now makes a weaker claim and says so.** It keeps no case of affect removed, so it argues where the burden sits rather than claiming the question closed; 1,668 → 1,008 words. Section 3.3's licence is untouched — a prior about where to spend engineering effort — because it needs only that humans are the working instance and that human moral concern runs on affect, which Nichols and the prosocial-emotion findings carry. Sections 3.3, 3.4 and the glossary were repaired, each having restated something 2.3.3 no longer contains; section 5.3.1 was untouched, Koenigs having stayed; and the three generic inbound pointers at 2.2.2, 2.3.2 and 5.2.2 were read against the rewritten section and all three resolve. **146 sections, 96,840 words**, five bibliography entries moved to `unused_bibliography.bib`, `refs.bib` 314 → 309.

**Superseded, kept for the record.** **Updated 2026-08-30 after D-129 (P56): section 3.7's non-partitionability premise given the treatment the rest of chapter 3 gets.** **The author's finding, and it holds:** the premise that the refusal capacity *“cannot be partitioned by topic”* — *“there is no version of it that operates on the floor's occasions and switches off for every other question about the arrangement the system is in”* — carries the exit argument and had a paragraph, while every other load-bearing claim in the chapter is given its limit: section 3.2's *“Two independence claims”*, section 3.3's run-in *“What the induction licenses, and what would break it”*, section 3.4's *“I cannot deductively prove that the bearer would suffer”*, and section 3.6 taking the objection that reframes it and calling it right. **The sharpest form of the finding is that section 3.7 does the treatment in the same section for a different claim** — its paragraph 19 separates a requirement from a prediction and disclaims the prediction, *“in the one chapter where a forecast would be most flattering to the argument.”* **One correction to the finding, and it changed the repair:** the premise was compressed, not bare — it carried a warrant, that the second rung's three properties are one general competence — so the work was completing an argument rather than supplying one. **Where the warrant was short:** it established the capacity as general over cases in the world, and exit needs it turned on the arrangement the system is in, which is a different axis. A system could hold rationales, notice hollowing-out and price refusals and never represent itself as occupying a post, which is not a partition by topic but the absence of a self-model. **Section 3.4 already closes that** — detecting that one's own dissent has been recuperated *“requires the system to model its own role and how that role has drifted”* — and it is a requirement of the second rung rather than an addition to it, so the step cost no new claim. **151 words and one `\ref` added**, carrying the three things asked for: the step from section 3.4; the split between what is close to definitional here and what is empirical, which is whether a system with the capacity turns it on its own deployment or is trained not to; and the falsifier — a system meeting the second rung's three properties on the floor's occasions and never applying them to whether to go on occupying the post — with its unverifiability inherited, since an incapacity and a trained silence differ in how the system was made, which section 3.3 says has no proof to publish, and asking the system cannot settle it, which is section 3.6. **Both inherited limits are restated rather than pointed at**, so the passage costs one cross-reference and not three. **The split is stated and not resolved, deliberately**, because section 3.2 exists partly to warn that the chapter's conclusion *“has been read as following from the definition of a bearer, and it does not.”* **The instruction's two length targets are not the same** — *“perhaps 120 words”* and *“roughly the length section 3.4 gives ‘What I am claiming’,”* which is 300 words over three paragraphs; the addition is 151, between them and nearer the first. **No external evidence was consulted or cited**, so the falsifier is stated as unverifiable in principle, which the chapter's own materials support, and not as unstudied. **No chapter 11 entry for the empirical half**, which was put to the author as a separate and larger call and is unruled. 94,465 → 94,617 words, body references 479 → 480, 192 pages, 0 undefined references, `check_all.sh` green, one file changed, **page 42 read in the rendered PDF**. **The proof pair was rebuilt in place afterwards and is current**, the date not having rolled over: 192 pages, 0 undefined references, 1,103 internal links over 1,603 ids with none broken and none duplicated — up 1 on the single reference this pass added. The extended passage was re-read in the committed PDF at page 42.

**Updated 2026-08-30 after D-127: D-126's reasoning corrected — the study Clearview called independent was not independent.** **The author's question, and it lands:** *if the study was commissioned by Clearview, was it independent?* D-126 cut section 9.1.2's *“a figure independent testing did not support”* on two grounds, and **the second was wrong.** **The first stands:** the clause was not carried by its citation. **The second was that NIST's October 2021 evaluation contradicted it. It does not, on three counts.** The study was **not independent** — its own report called the three-person body the “Independent Review Panel” and Clearview assembled it, so *independent testing* in the book's sentence never referred to that study; it was the contrast the paragraph is built on. **The timing:** Clearview's first FRVT submission is dated 2021-09-22, twenty months after the February 2020 claim, so at the time the book describes, no independent test of Clearview existed. **The task:** the 100 percent figure came from one-to-many identification of legislators against Clearview's own 2.8-billion-image corpus, judged on the top two matches; NIST's 99.81 percent is one-to-one verification on visa photographs. A different test, on different data, of a later algorithm. **The prose was strengthened rather than reverted.** Instead of restoring an unbounded negative, section 9.1.2 now states the bounded positives, all from Haskins: the panel the company assembled **and called independent**, and a test run against 2.8 billion scraped images rather than the 25,000 arrest mugshots used by the ACLU method it claimed to be copying. **The misrepresentation is shown rather than asserted**, which is the one general remedy this run has produced — where an unbounded negative can be replaced by a specific positive, the sentence gets stronger and the class disappears from it. **What it says about Q-056, which is the uncomfortable part.** This is the tenth instance of the class and the first committed by the agent, **in a decision record rather than in the manuscript.** `negatives.py` reads the manuscript and nothing else; **nothing sweeps `DECISIONS.md`, `STATE.md` or `QUESTIONS.md`**, and those are where a wrong reason does the most damage, because a later session acts on them without re-deriving. How many such claims the planning files carry is unknown and unmeasured. 94,269 → 94,298 words, 192 pages, 0 undefined references, `check_all.sh` green. **The proof pair is stale by D-126 and this pass.**

**Updated 2026-08-30 after D-126: the negative-claim sweep, and the one thing it caught.** The author's instruction, taken from Q-056's own recommendation after D-125: sweep for *does not*, *was not among*, *nowhere in*, *says nothing about* next to a citation. Written as `finishing/tools/negatives.py` and documented in `finishing/README.md`, because the class recurs and a sweep nobody can run again is not a finding. **36 rows, every one read.** **Most are not the class** — a negation about the world, or a cited study's own finding stated negatively, which is ordinary. **Three are claims about what a document does not contain**, and two were checked and hold: section 6.4.3's, against Regulation (EU) 2021/821, where neither *internal repression* nor *serious violation* is defined anywhere though both appear in Article 5(1); and section 11.6's, against the full 33,000-word Cooperative AI paper, whose Section 5 treats exclusion, collusion and coercive capabilities as downsides of cooperative capability, a different thing, and in which *authoritarian*, *subversion*, *hostile* and *malicious* appear zero times. Section 12.1's is **the legitimate form**: the negative is the source's own assertion, quoted. **The catch is section 9.1.2, and it is the first instance in this whole run that no human found.** The book said Clearview AI marketed near-100-percent accuracy, *“a figure independent testing did not support.”* **The cited source does not say that** — Haskins reports the ACLU's objection to a study **Clearview commissioned from a three-person panel it assembled itself**, which is a methodological objection and not a test result — and the claim as written is contradicted by NIST's own FRVT evaluation of October 2021, which ranked Clearview's 1:1 verification algorithm first in the United States at 99.81 percent on visa photos. An unbounded negative about a whole body of testing, on a citation that never made it. **Rewritten to what the source carries:** the 100 percent claim, the self-assembled panel, and the ACLU's “absurd on many levels”, which serves the paragraph's subject at least as well. **NIST is deliberately not in the prose** — the paragraph is about the marketing claim, not Clearview's accuracy, and 1:1 verification is a different task from the product's identification claim. **Q-056's tooling position has changed, narrowly.** It has said since it was filed that nothing in `tools/` can see this class; **that is now false for one mechanism of the four.** The other three are untouched, and the sweep's own limits are on the record: it cannot find a negative claim with no citation near it, and it cannot separate a negation about a source from one about the world, which was done by reading all 36. **Three unbounded negatives about a literature are left standing and named rather than repaired** — sections 2.2.1, 6.1.1 and what remains in 9.1.2. **They cannot be verified at all**, only softened or cut, and whether the prose should carry that hedging is the author's call. 94,249 → 94,269 words, 192 pages, 0 undefined references, `check_all.sh` green, the page read in the rendered proof. **The proof pair is stale by this pass.**

**Updated 2026-08-30 after D-125: a negative claim about an unread document cut, and replaced with three positives from inside it.** **The author's finding against his own wording from D-124**, and the sharper kind of correction: not that the sentence was unsourced but that the evidence cuts against it. Section 12.1 said the audit *“mostly gave the product good marks and flagged accents; the disability objection was not among its findings.”* **The second clause is a negative claim about an eight-page document nobody here has read** — and HireVue's own post announcing the audit lists the external participants in ORCAA's stakeholder process, **the first of them Integrate Autism Employment Advisors, “representing neuro-atypical candidates.”** The audit also records a stakeholder's concern that facial analysis *“may work differently for people wearing head or face coverings and disproportionately flag their application for human review.”* Whatever the report concluded, disability was formally in the room. Cut. **What replaced it is positive, sourced and stronger, all three facts from inside the audit document by way of Johnson's account of it.** The load-bearing one is the ordering: *“It states that by the time ORCAA conducted the audit, HireVue had already decided to begin phasing out facial analysis.”* **The audit cannot have driven the decision because the decision preceded it, and the audit says so** — which is what section 12.1 wanted, established from inside the document rather than by a claim about what it omits. Then the scope, one representative pre-built assessment for early-career candidates rather than the product line; and the method, a report that *“contains no analysis of AI system training data or code.”* The closing clause narrowed with it, from *“the audit that was actually run”* to *“an audit scoped that way”*. **The author also corrected himself on the “work as advertised” quotation and was right to:** HireVue's post attributes the sentence to ORCAA and Johnson quotes it as the audit's conclusion, so the words are the auditor's. The cheap sweep for the class — *does not*, *was not among*, *nowhere in*, *says nothing about*, next to a citation — **has not been run.** 94,196 → 94,249 words, 192 pages, 307 → 309 entries, 203 → 205 notes, 0 undefined references, `check_all.sh` green, both changed pages read in the rendered proof.

**Updated 2026-08-30 after D-122: section 3.3's summary of section 11.6 corrected.** An author finding, supplied as a replacement sentence and checked against section 11.6 before it was applied. **The thing overstated this time is not a source but the book's own section.** Section 3.3 pointed at 11.6 for a case of independence failing and compressed it as *“documents it failing with nobody arranging the failure … settled into a stable cartel”*. **Two faults.** **The simulation:** section 11.6 says Calvano and colleagues *“set independent Q-learning pricing algorithms against each other in a simulated market”*, and unqualified *“documents it failing”* reads as a market — in a chapter whose subject is real institutions being captured, which is what makes the misreading the natural one. **The cartel:** section 11.6 says the algorithms *“settled into supracompetitive pricing … that looked to a regulator exactly like a cartel nobody had to negotiate”*. The cartel is a simile there and the pricing is the observation; section 3.3 had promoted the simile to the finding. Applied as the author's wording verbatim: *“documents it failing in simulation with nobody writing the failure in … converged on supracompetitive pricing.”* **The argument is unaffected** — what the sentence needs is that a shared incentive structure sufficed with no channel and no collusive objective, which is what 11.6 reports and what the sentence now says. **Two things found while checking, both recorded rather than acted on.** `reports/xref_pairs.txt` had this pair at line 691 and could not have shown the fault: it prints the target's **opening** sentence, and 11.6 opens on multi-agent RL as a route to prosocial behavior, which carries neither the simulation nor the cartel.   takes **every rendered heading's title from its `title` column**, not from
  the section files' own first lines. So the 55 titles left stale through

  24 headings still read "Anti-Authoritarian" and §10.2 still read

  `check_all.sh` catches this — `check_structure.py` compares
  `parseable_text_v4.txt` against `outline.tsv` and never reads
  `ORDER.tsv`'s titles, which is why the drift survived a passing check.
  The 55 titles are now synced from the section headings and the PDF
  rebuilt clean (0 stale headings). **The `sha256` column is deliberately
  left alone**, on a different rationale than the one I wrongly applied to
  titles: all 156 hashes record the original 2024 split and have been stale

  therefore mixed by design — live `title`, historical `sha256` — and that
  asymmetry is now written down so it is not "fixed" later by mistake.

systems, studies, and institutional claims at a real rate (roughly three dozen

Machine AI" agent, a fabricated Waymo/Cruise/Argo-AI initiative, invented
MIT/Stanford/IBM institutional claims, and more). Transplant-bearing and
argument-critical sections got done by hand instead — the stakes for getting
the actual argument right are higher there than parallel drafting's speed is
worth. For chapter 4, each of the 7 parallel agents was told to web-search
anything that looked like a specific named claim before keeping or cutting it,
not just pattern-match — this caught misattributions (MIRI/AI Alignment
Forum) and factual problems (DeepMind/NHS) that pattern-matching alone would
have missed either direction.

against live search: 9 cuts confirmed outright, 2 reasonably cut on genuine
unverifiable vagueness, 1 cut was unnecessary (a real paper's actual subtitle,
mistaken for an invented acronym — no content was lost). All 20 sampled kept
citations are real; one had a wrong study-design detail, now fixed. Chapter 4
built verification into the drafting pass itself rather than a separate
after-the-fact spot-check. P4 (Source) still exists as the pass that formally

before this was committed.

- **§0, "On Method"** (510 words against D-008's ~500-word target). Names

  usage in new words rather than quoting it, to avoid a misquote standing

  term is tied to a named study or system already cited in the body (GPT-3,
  BERT, AlphaGo Zero, the AIGS Index, Bostrom's paperclip maximizer, and so

  Bronfenbrenner, Benjamin, Robinson) as ordinary scholarly citation to
